tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Homology of CW skeleton pairs] ↗ def:cell-complex 1. ch2:2.34\group Cellular Homology

For a CW complex $X$:

  1. $H_k(X^n,X^{n-1})=0$ for $k\ne n$, while $H_n(X^n,X^{n-1})$ is free on the $n$-cells;

  2. $H_k(X^n)=0$ for $k>n$;

  3. $H_k(X^n)\to H_k(X)$ is an isomorphism for $k<n$ and is surjective for $k=n$.

Consequently, if $X$ is finite-dimensional, then $H_k(X)=0$ for $k>\dim X$.
Proof

\sketch The quotient $X^n/X^{n-1}$ is a wedge of $n$-spheres. The pair exact sequence gives the skeletal vanishing and stabilization maps. For arbitrary $X$, every finite singular cycle and bounding chain has compact image and lies in a finite skeleton, so the stabilized skeletal groups compute $H_k(X)$.

□

The cellular chain complex is \[ \cdots \to H_n(X^n,X^{n-1})\xrightarrow {d_n}H_{n-1}(X^{n-1},X^{n-2})\to \cdots , \qquad d_n=j_{n-1}\partial _n. \] Its homology is denoted $H_n^{CW}(X)$.
